notes.title: Dedup engine — design decisions log
notes.content:
Aug 12: Started circulating the dedup design doc. Key tension: throughput vs. dedup accuracy.
Aug 14: Sam raised fingerprint collision concern at 1M events/min. Need to re-examine the key composition.
Aug 17: Switched to SHA-256 composite key — (source, rule_id, host, 15min_window). Modelling shows collision probability < 1 in 10^18 at peak load. Problem solved.
Aug 19: Design locked after Morgan approved v4.
Sep 3: Load tests showing single-shard Redis bottleneck at 950K events/min. Lab spike on Redis Cluster mode looking good — 1.35M events/min at p99 18ms. Will adopt cluster mode for production.

notes.title: AWS migration — architecture notes
notes.content:
Aug 19: Steering committee approved capacity plan: 3×r6i.4xlarge + ALB for ingestion tier. Target cutover W42.
Aug 20: Need to decide network topology before W37 — Jordan is the decision-maker.
Sep 1: Transit Gateway chosen over VPC peering. Rationale: TGW simplifies multi-account expansion. Prism will need 3 AWS accounts by EOY; VPC peering mesh gets unwieldy past 2-3 accounts.
Sep 3: TGW provisioned in dev. Connectivity tests pass. Staging next.

notes.title: Q3 retro notes
notes.content:
Sep 2: Architecture review done. Leadership bought in on both dedup engine and migration roadmap.
	Key feedback from exec: dedup p99 target (20ms) is right — don't relax it.
	Risk flagged: Redis single-shard bottleneck could delay Phase 1. Cluster mode is the fix; adds ops complexity but unavoidable at this scale.
Sep 3: Starting to think about Q4 scope. Signal normalisation layer is the natural next piece after dedup — needed to handle multi-source ingestion properly.
